name: Coarse Geometric Karchmer-Wigderson (CG-KW)

primitives.name: KW-metric space
primitives.type: finite metric space (X_f, d_f) with X_f = f^{-1}(0) ⊔ f^{-1}(1)
primitives.description: For a boolean function f:{0,1}^n -> {0,1}, define d_f(x,y) = log_2(min number of coordinates a depth-bounded distinguisher must read to certify f(x) ≠ f(y), or +∞ if f(x)=f(y) and they lie in the same coarse component). Computable by a finite enumeration over coordinate subsets; gives a quasi-metric on inputs that the KW protocol must navigate.

primitives.name: Controlled cover
primitives.type: finite family U = {U_i ⊂ X_f} with diameter bound R
primitives.description: A cover whose parts have d_f-diameter at most R and whose overlap multiplicity is at most m. Encoded as a hypergraph H_U (vertices = X_f, edges = U_i). Inspired by Gromov's asymptotic dimension and Roe's controlled coverings.

primitives.name: Coarse cocycle
primitives.type: function c : X_f × X_f -> Z with finite support modulo controlled equivalence
primitives.description: A discrete 1-cochain in the Roe-style coarse cohomology HX^*(X_f) restricted to the KW pair structure. Stored as a sparse table on pairs (x,y) with d_f(x,y) ≤ R; coboundary computable by a triangle sum δc(x,y,z) = c(y,z) - c(x,z) + c(x,y).

primitives.name: Asymptotic-dimension witness
primitives.type: vertex coloring χ : X_f -> [k] together with diameter bound R
primitives.description: Witnesses asdim(X_f) ≤ k-1 in the sense of Gromov: each color class decomposes into d_f-bounded pieces of diameter ≤ R that are pairwise R-disjoint. Computable by greedy R-net construction (Bell-Dranishnikov style).

primitives.name: Roe-controlled operator
primitives.type: matrix T ∈ R^{X_f × X_f} with T_{x,y} = 0 whenever d_f(x,y) > R
primitives.description: Element of the algebraic uniform Roe algebra C_u^*[X_f]. Stored as a banded sparse matrix in the d_f-metric; multiplication, adjoint, and trace are all polynomial-time in |X_f|.

operations.name: coarse_product
operations.description: Models block composition f ∘ g (à la Karchmer-Raz-Wigderson). The product metric is d_{f∘g} = d_f ⊕ d_g with a 'depth-additive' coupling controlled by coarse Lipschitz maps.

operations.name: controlled_refinement
operations.description: Refine a controlled cover by intersecting with a finer R'-net. Decreases diameter; may increase multiplicity. Tracks the growth function R ↦ multiplicity(U_R), which is the asymptotic-dimension-control function.

operations.name: coboundary
operations.description: Discrete coarse-cohomology differential δ. Computable on sparse tables; kernels and images give HX^k(X_f). We focus on HX^1 (obstruction to ‘flattening’ the KW game by a constant-depth protocol).

operations.name: reduction_pullback
operations.description: A coarse-Lipschitz reduction induces a pullback on cocycles and on Roe-controlled operators; this is the categorical glue that lets lower bounds transfer.

operations.name: asymptotic_completion
operations.description: Take a Gromov-Hausdorff / ultralimit over the family {f_n} of n-bit instances to obtain a 'limit space' on which infinite asymptotic invariants live. Implemented operationally via a finite-truncation oracle.

operations.name: trace_pairing
operations.description: Index-theoretic pairing ⟨c, T⟩ = tr(c · T) (in the sense of Roe's index pairing, after Connes). This is the quantitative bridge from cohomology classes to formula-depth lower bounds.

target_invariant.name: Coarse depth κ(f)
target_invariant.what_it_should_bound: κ(f) := sup over nontrivial c ∈ HX^1(X_f) and T ∈ C_u^*[X_f] of log|⟨c,T⟩| / log(propagation(T)). The conjecture is depth(f) ≥ κ(f), so a super-logarithmic κ(f) for an explicit f gives a super-logarithmic formula-depth lower bound (a P ⊄ NC^1 separation if κ is poly-large).

axioms_tentative: A1 (Coarse-KW link): formula depth d(f) ≥ Ω(log(asdim(X_f))) and more strongly d(f) ≥ Ω(κ(f)); proved by translating a KW protocol into a controlled cover whose multiplicity exponent equals depth.
A2 (Composition sub-additivity): asdim(X_{f∘g}) ≥ asdim(X_f) + asdim(X_g) − O(1), giving a KRW-style direct-sum theorem at the level of coarse dimension.

A3 (Anti-natural-proofs): for a uniformly random f, HX^1(X_f) is generically zero (Roe-algebraic concentration of measure), so κ is NOT a 'largeness' property in the Razborov-Rudich sense — random f's have small κ, blocking natural-proofs obstructions.

A4 (Anti-relativization): κ is a metric invariant of d_f and is destroyed by oracle access (oracle gates collapse d_f to ≤ 1), so κ-based bounds cannot relativize, in the spirit of Mendel-Naor metric cotype obstructions.

A5 (Roe-index rigidity): nontrivial classes in HX^1(X_f) detected by the Roe-trace pairing are stable under coarse equivalence, mirroring Yu's coarse Baum-Connes results (Yu 2000; Nowak-Yu 2012); explicit candidate functions (Andreev's, element-distinctness) are conjectured to realize κ = Ω(log^2 n)
